[h3] Absolutely charming, a total masterpiece! [/h3] Everything in this little game is handmade. You can tell right away. The monsters, items and overall assets have a really fresh clay touch that I just can't stop praising. Seriously, someone stop me. But what about the game itself? Is it solid? Hell, yes it is! It's a roguelike, so if you die you start from scratch, but you earn medals and unlock things that help you along the way. It's also varied. You start with different starters, explore biomes in different orders, and as well as battles there are chests with items, upgrades and shops. The monsters not only get captured, they also evolve and you can choose from tons of abilities with funny names and descriptions. It's in early access and gets frequent updates, so I didn't wait for a sale and bought it at full price, and I'm very glad I did.
I stayed up past my bedtime to play this.

If the definition of the phrase "labor of love" could have an image next to it I think this game could be it. The culmination of a lifelong passion for sculpting and indie games, this game scratches all the itches a turn based strategy fan might have and then some. It's Slay the Spire meets Pokemon Stadium, minus the corporate greed and mid-tier art (THE ART IS ACTUAL SCULPTURES DAWG, like come on! S-Tier!). Don't be such a brokie and sink your teeth into this gem.

Very cool game. The roguelike experience has been very engaging and well-balanced so far, and the humor is top notch. There's definitely a lot of bugs (like items taking up ghost slots in your inventory), but even accounting for them, this is still an 8/10 for me. If you like Pokemon but want a more engaging gameplay loop, give this a shot.

Anything with handmade assets immediately gets a +5 to the rating in the age of AI garbage. And this game easily gets a good rating even without that boost. Super charming sprites, a good sense of humor, interesting moves and mechanics... And honestly the best of all is that the Sculplings don't feel like Temu Pokemon, they actually have their own identity. I played for an hour with no bugs or other issues. Right now I'd say my biggest request would be a game speed button so we could crank this thang up to 11 and speed through a bunch of runs. At default speed, some of the animations and text boxes linger a biiiit too long for my liking. Not annoying right now, but if I put another 100 hours into this game my brain would be melting over how long it takes to gain XP after a fight

This is a gem amongst creature collectors. I've played many Pokémon games, rom hacks, SMT, Persona, Digimon World3, even Dragon Quest Monsters, so I've played quite a few games of this genre. Even so, this game managed to stand out with its unique presentation and engaging combat. In a world dominated by LLM generated content, it is very refreshing to see someone designing the creatures literally by hand, which gives this game a silly vibe that communicates very well with its humor, which I love. The creature design is very cute and silly, even the scenary was handcrafted with faces, so there is a lot of effort on that regard, which I really appreciate. I've found that many creature collector games try too much to reproduce Pokémon's creature design, which kinda turns me off, and this game has a different approach that makes it unique. The combat is Pokémon, which is excepted from this kind of games, but the roguelite elements give it a very fresh air. Basically, you do runs where you can caught sculplings up to 4 at a time, get items, upgrades, even increase stats or teach new moves. This prevents the player from always building the same team and force to strategize with whatever the game throws to the player. I'm still far from collecting all sculplings, but it is such a joy trying to guess how it is going to evolve. There is no story, you get to challenge tough trainer until becoming the #1, there is a edgy rival and other cliches, but it works. I know I compared this a lot with Pokémon, but it is kinda of the gold standard, and this game succeeded into differentiating it from so many creature collections inspired by game freak's franchise. If you like creature collectors and roguelikes, you will love this.

Reworked the review to go into detail, as I didn't see other reviews having done so. It is worth a mention that the game contains cussing and some more "adult" themes, so despite the visuals, I may not suggest the game to the youngest in the family. Has a lot going for it, but various things make me hesitant to recommend it. + Charming + Funny (though humor is on-the-nose a lot, but I like it) + Good price + Devs seem to be working on fixes + Decent amount of depth/builds + You get to pick 1 starter out of 3 every run * Meta-progression, you earn more slots for more team passives to start with as well as unlock mostly stronger items to appear during the run. Beating bosses also upgrades the passive beating them unlocked - Lack of polish. Visual oddities, jank and minor bugs. These aren't show stoppers but they certainly take wind out of the sails - Game's progression involves fighting Top 5 rank bosses, which have unique mechanics that aren't really told of ahead of the time, so you may end up failing a run learning their gimmick the hard way - Balance. Sometimes an enemy has a move that instantly kills my creature, which they can use multiple times, I have beaten the game but I still don't know what that move is or how to counteract it, this has been rare but it happens - Item bloat. As you unlock more passives and items to show up, it becomes increasingly harder to find what you want. Chests on the map have no reroll option (though enemy drops let you reroll them) - RNG. Learned moves are random as are item drops, bosses encountered, regular encounters, hit chance... this can cause frustrating moments at times - Same currency that is used for items during the run is used to unlock permanent things, so at times I end up tanking the run in favor of keeping more cash Game works for the most part, but all the small things stop the experience from becoming something I could recommend easily. Still, I can see people enjoying it.
